# Gold V1 — H5 data-quality gate

**Result: DATA QUALITY PASS**, 15 of 15 checks. The machine record is `data_quality.json`, regenerated by
`h5_study.py` on every run; the study aborts on any failure.

## Before computing H5

- **Earlier studies intact:** H1, H2 and H3 were verified byte-identical to their closed state (SHA-256).
- **Existing tests pass:** 22/22 before any H5 code was written. The existing test files are unchanged.
- **Frozen code untouched:** no frozen P3.1/P2.x code was touched.

## Rerun corrected H1 gate (checks 1–12)

All 12 pass on the same development rows (10,355 M15 bars, 2025-12-23 00:00 → 2026-06-02 23:45 UTC). The evidence
is in `../h1/data_quality.md`.

## H5 additions

| check | result | method |
|---|---|---|
| h5_or_dst_mapping | PASS | Every one of the 113 opening ranges starts at 09:30 New York. That is 14:30 UTC on the 52 EST days and 13:30 UTC on the 61 EDT days (US DST from 2026-03-08). No fixed UTC offset is used; bars are selected by `zoneinfo` wall-clock time. |
| h5_or_causal | PASS | For every event: the OR is exactly the max/min of the 09:30 and 09:45 bars; both confirming closes come after the OR, from 10:00 New York; the confirming bar starts between 10:15 and 12:45 New York; entry is the next bar; the stop is the OR midpoint. |
| h5_prefix_invariance | PASS | Events recomputed on the first 70% of rows equal the full run inside the prefix. |

## Regression tests

The new file is `research/gold_v1/tests/test_h5.py`, with 11 tests; the existing test files are unchanged. The whole
suite runs:

```
venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider research/gold_v1/tests
```

It passes 33/33.

| test | what it pins |
|---|---|
| `test_opening_range_maps_to_correct_utc_bars_across_dst` | **The dedicated DST test.** On synthetic broker sessions on 03-05, 03-06, 03-09 and 03-10, the 09:30–10:00 New York range maps to 14:30/14:45 UTC before the US DST change and 13:30/13:45 UTC after it. The OR high/low equal those bars' max/min. |
| `test_ny_minutes` (6 cases) | UTC → New York wall-clock minutes in EST and EDT, including the last confirming bar (12:45 New York) in January and May |
| `test_two_consecutive_strict_closes_needed_and_equality_is_not_outside` | a close equal to OR high is not outside; an inside close resets the streak; confirmation needs two adjacent strict closes |
| `test_one_event_per_direction_and_both_directions_kept` | the repeat in the same direction is suppressed; the opposite direction is kept and flagged; the stop is the OR midpoint |
| `test_no_confirmation_after_1245_new_york` | outside closes at 12:45 and 13:00 New York cannot confirm |
| `test_future_perturbation_does_not_change_past_events` | noise added to the second half of the sample leaves every earlier event unchanged, including `first_break` and `opposite_swept_before` |

## Data notes specific to H5

- **Days without an OR.** The one trading day without an OR is the partial day that begins 2026-06-02 22:00 UTC, which
  the development cut truncates. Good Friday (2026-04-03) is not a trading day in the data.
- **Short sessions.** Four OR days have an early close before 16:45 New York; they are flagged `us_short_session`. US
  equity holidays (MLK, Presidents Day, Memorial Day) still have a gold OR and are included.
- **Extreme bars.** 2026-01-29 15:00–15:30 UTC is a genuine ~400-point crash, with consistent M15 and H1 bars and very
  high tick volume. The resulting event (risk 6.4 ATR) is kept.
- **Thin control pool.** The ±8-bar exclusion removes most of the 3-hour signal window on event days. Only 139 unique
  control bars stand behind 490 draws; see the report.
